class.name: TressFXHair
class.brief_description: A GPU-simulated hair or fur object (AMD TressFX).
class.description: Loads a [code].tfx[/code] hair asset, simulates its guide strands on the GPU every frame, keeps them out of every [TressFXCollisionMesh] listed in [member collision_meshes] and draws the strands as camera-facing ribbons. With a [member hair_skeleton] and a [code].tfxbone[/code] file the hair is skinned to the animated skeleton; without a skeleton it follows this node rigidly. The node simulates in the editor too: move the skeleton or scrub its animation and the hair follows. When nothing has changed for a few seconds the editor simulation sleeps until the next change. Requires the Forward+ or Mobile renderer (the Compatibility renderer has no [RenderingDevice]). Look and lighting settings live in a [ShaderMaterial] using [code]addons/tressfx/shaders/tressfx_strand.gdshader[/code], see [member material]. [b]Note:[/b] Use MSAA 4x together with TAA: the strands are rendered with alpha-to-coverage, and TAA turns the dithered edges into a soft volume.

method.name: capture_positions
method.description: Debug helper: queues a readback of the simulated vertex positions from the GPU. The result is available from [method get_captured_positions] on the following frame. Reading back stalls the GPU, do not call it every frame in a shipped game.

method.name: get_captured_positions
method.description: Returns the positions captured by the last [method capture_positions] call, four floats per vertex (x, y, z, and 0 for pinned vertices) in world space, guide and follow strands interleaved.

method.name: get_cpu_time_usec
method.description: Main-thread time spent by this node in the last frame, in microseconds (bone matrices, parameters and command recording; the simulation itself runs on the GPU).

method.name: get_guide_strand_count
method.description: Number of simulated guide strands, padded to a multiple of 64.

method.name: get_strand_count
method.description: Number of drawn strands: guide strands times ([member num_follow_hairs] + 1).

method.name: get_vertex_count
method.description: Total number of hair vertices, guide and follow strands included.

method.name: get_vertices_per_strand
method.description: Vertices per strand as stored in the [code].tfx[/code] file (4, 8, 16, 32 or 64).

method.name: reset_positions
method.description: Snaps the hair back to its rest pose over the next two frames. Call it after teleporting the character so the hair does not fly across the level.

members.member: Whether the strands cast shadows. Off by default: a million ribbon triangles in every shadow cascade is the single most expensive thing the hair can do.
Maximum distance a vertex may move in one frame. Keeps the simulation from exploding after a very long frame.
Signed distance fields the guide strands are pushed out of after every simulation step. Every listed mesh is applied every frame.

Vertices at the root of each strand that never collide (the first two are pinned anyway). Raise it for grooms whose roots sit inside the collider: a strand pushed at its base every frame swings outwards as a whole.
Velocity damping per frame. The AMD sample uses 0.068; 0.2 brings fur fully to rest.
Spread of the follow hairs around their guide strand, in metres. Changing it reloads the asset.
Fraction of each strand, from the root, that the global shape constraint applies to.
How strongly the first [member global_range] of every strand is pulled back to the authored rest shape. Keeps a hairstyle's parting and volume; lower it for a tail that must swing as a mass.
Gravity acceleration. The shape constraints are position based, so a strong gravity fights them and the hair never settles; the AMD sample uses 0.09, long hair around 1.
Skeleton the hair is skinned to, using the bone names in [member tfxbone_path]. Without a skeleton the hair follows this node rigidly. Changing it reloads the asset.
Multiplies the [code].tfx[/code] positions on load; use 0.01 for an asset authored in centimetres. Changing it reloads the asset.
Iterations of the segment length constraint per frame.
Iterations of the local shape constraint per frame.
How strongly each segment keeps its authored bend relative to the previous one (curls, waves).

Distance LOD: the strands are dealt into four meshes that fade out one by one between [member lod_start_distance] and [member lod_end_distance], while the remaining fibers widen by [member lod_width_multiplier] to keep the coverage.
Distance at which only [member lod_percent] of the strands remain.
Fraction of strands still drawn at [member lod_end_distance] and beyond (rounded to quarters).
Distance at which strands start to drop out.
Fiber width multiplier reached at [member lod_end_distance].

Material using [code]tressfx_strand.gdshader[/code]; colour, fiber radius and lighting live there. Without one a default material is created. Use one material per hair node: the node writes its simulated positions texture and vertex count into the material's shader parameters.
Follow strands generated around every guide strand. Follow strands are not simulated, they are offset copies of their guide, so they are almost free. Changing it reloads the asset.

Keep simulating while the hair is hidden or outside the current camera's view. Off by default: hair nobody can see sleeps, and colliders no hair used last frame are not rebuilt. After a long sleep the hair snaps to its rest pose instead of flying to the character's new position.
Distance from the camera beyond which the hair stops simulating, in metres (0 = never). Combine with [member lod_enabled]: far away hair is drawn with fewer strands and frozen in its last pose.
The [code].tfx[/code] file with the guide strands (4 to 64 vertices per strand, a power of two). Changing it reloads the asset.
Optional [code].tfxbone[/code] file with the bone weights of every guide strand; bone names must exist in [member hair_skeleton]. Changing it reloads the asset.
How much further the follow hairs spread towards the tip (0 keeps them parallel to their guide).
Root acceleration above which the velocity shock propagation coefficient is forced to 1 so a violent head move cannot pull the hair apart.
Velocity shock propagation: how much of the root's rigid motion is copied onto the whole strand. High values make the hair a helmet, low values let it lag and swing.
Direction the wind blows towards.
Wind acceleration, same units as [member gravity]; it gusts between half and one and a half times this value. Fur bends visibly around 1 to 3.
